claims.claim: A voter must be registered to vote to apply for a proxy vote.
claims.quote: You and your proxy must both be registered to vote in the UK before you can apply.

claims.claim: Proxy voting is available when a voter cannot attend a polling station in person.
claims.quote: You can get someone else to vote on your behalf (a proxy) if you cannot go to the polling station in person.

claims.claim: Being away for work can be a reason for a proxy vote.
Illness can be a reason for a proxy vote.
claims.quote: having a medical issue or disability

claims.claim: Being abroad can be a reason for a proxy vote.
claims.quote: If you want to vote by proxy and you live abroad, apply for a proxy vote as soon as possible.

claims.claim: Disability can be a reason for a proxy vote.
The proxy must be a registered UK voter.
claims.quote: You and your proxy must both be registered to vote in the UK before you can apply.

claims.claim: The standard proxy deadline is six working days before the election.
claims.quote: You must apply by: 5pm, 6 working days before election day in England, Scotland or Wales 5pm, 14 working days before election day in Northern Ireland
claims.note: The six-working-day deadline is for England, Scotland and Wales; Northern Ireland has a 14-working-day deadline.

claims.claim: An emergency proxy can be requested after the standard deadline.
claims.quote: If the proxy vote deadline has passed you may be able to apply for an emergency proxy vote

claims.claim: An emergency proxy can be requested until 5pm on polling day.
claims.quote: In England, Scotland and Wales, you have until 5pm on the day of the election to apply.
claims.note: The 5pm election-day deadline applies in England, Scotland and Wales, while Northern Ireland does not offer an emergency proxy.
